*Beijing* (Ice). Commentary: When one treads upon hoarfrost, one should know that the Yin energy is gradually increasing until it reaches solid ice.
This is like a petty person who, though initially very slight, grows until they reach full power. ○ *Dingzhong* (Top of the Head and Heels) and *Juan'ai* (A Drop and A Particle) both appear above.
○ *Rizhong* (Midday): The *Yi* says, "Abundant prosperity; the King approaches it; do not worry; it is appropriate for midday. The *Tuan* says: "The Sun..."

When midday arrives, the sun declines; when the moon is full, it wanes. The filling and emptying of heaven and earth correspond to the waxing and waning of the seasons. Regarding the calamity of eclipses, the *Táng lèi hán* states:

"The mutual occultations of the sun and moon are the disasters of heaven and earth. Regarding being cast into ditches and ravines, Mencius said: "In years of famine and scarcity, the old and weak among Your Majesty’s people are cast into ditches and ravines.

Regarding the "Bǎn" and "Dàn" [odes]: [The *Shī jīng* says: "The great state is in peril; the people are distressed. The ruler does not know his own faults, yet he seeks counsel from others. "The state is in chaos; the people are in distress. The ruler does not know his own faults, yet he seeks counsel from others."
The *Commentary on the Mao Shi* states: "Bǎnbǎn" means perverse; "tángtáng" describes the appearance of the collapse and ruin of laws and measures.

Regarding the sincerity of "offering the sun's warmth," see the previous section. As for the "Turtle-Pillar" (*Àoji*), the *Liezi* says: "In ancient times, the Lady Nüwa smelted stones of five colors to mend the breach in heaven;
she severed the feet of a giant turtle to establish the four poles. "Earth and Heaven interact in Tai" refers to the hexagram *Tai*.
The *Yi* says in the *Tuan* of *Tai*: "In *Tai*, the small departs and the great arrives; there is good fortune and success. This means that heaven and earth interact and all things are unimpeded.
[The hexagrams] *Da You* and "Hanging Images" are both seen above.
The Memorial for the Universal Deliverance on the Middle Primordial (Zhongyuan), written for General Inspector Gu.
We prostrate and reflect: The sacred scriptures are widely opened on this day of the Buddhas’ Great Joy;

our spiritual essence looks upward to reach them, manifesting the benevolence of universal compassion to wash away the transgressions of the past and universally uproot the bitter poisons of the dark gates of the underworld. Desiring...

The cultivation of wholesome fruits must necessarily rely upon worldly rituals. Now, based on the circumstances of the official of such-and-such a place named [Name], he reflects deeply that the winds of karma have caused him to drift and the moon of his wisdom has become obscured.

Having served in office for a long time, it is difficult to avoid the grievance of wrongful execution; having undertaken affairs with great hardship, there are likewise the faults of excessive injury.
Moreover, as he encounters the onset of an era of slaughter, he witnesses fully the suffering of the people, with corpses lying scattered across the land.
Throughout the vast fields, all is left to the ravages of rats and the scavenging of crows; white bones reach to the heavens, exposed to the full force of wind and sun.
The calamity of slaughter has not yet ceased, and the disaster of the great flood arises alongside it. Fields and dwellings are half-submerged by the surging waves;

men and women have for the most part been transformed into fish and turtles. To escape the extreme sufferings of the Nine Dark Realms, one must rely upon the vast compassion of the Triple Gem. By means of this...

We respectfully select the [day] of the seventh month in the year [year] to inaugurate at [Name] Temple a seven-day and seven-night *zhongyuan* ritual for relieving the obscure and uprooting suffering.
We shall prostrate before the twenty-four sections of the Liang Dynasty Imperial Repentance Sutra (*liáng huáng chǎn fǎ*).

At dawn, we shall chant the esoteric chapters and solemnly purify the altar and its precincts. We pray that the numinous power of the celestial generals may descend to suppress the demonic armies, and we beseech the Universal...
The King of Sages, sovereign of the noble vow, has descended to guide us like an elephant-king. Having manifested the signs of transgression throughout ten scrolls, he has spread forth his teachings;
I now prostrate with my whole heart before his vast and magnificent name. Plucking chrysanthemums and brewing tea, I offer these humble tokens as a ritual of service to all beings.

Drawing water and burning sandalwood incense, they merely manifest the reverence of one with a full jar; having completed the rites of *caṇḍamā* (confession), they further recite the texts of Kṣitigarbha.
At midday, they extensively prepare offerings of the three virtues and universally honor the Jewel of the Sangha from the ten directions.
When the crimson disk of the sun sinks in the west and the bright moon rises in the east, they invite the Vajra Master to ascend the Dharma seat and perform the *yoga*.
The profound efficacy of the *gamiti* mantra spreads far and wide; the clouds of Dharma-food gather like mists, instantly quelling the suffering of hunger and emptiness.
A rain of ambrosia falls, suddenly removing the cruelty of blazing heat. Relying solely on this humble sincerity, I look upward with hope for compassionate discernment.

I prostrate myself and pray that sunken souls and lingering spirits may transcend and ascend through the power of repentance; that the shackles of karma and the flowers of transgression may be instantly dissolved through the merit of the mantra. Golden Hall...
Within, you constantly behold the countenance of the purple-gold [Buddha]; at the heart of the azure pond’s waves, you occasionally hear the verses on suffering and emptiness.

We pray once more that the official so-and-so may be granted great fortune and a long life; may the light of your ever-prospering and flourishing achievements further increase the imperial favor bestowed upon you from Heaven.
We joyfully behold the decree of your honorable promotion and receive extensively this extraordinary felicity. Abundant blessings gather at your gate like a river flowing ever fuller;

auspicious celebrations shall flow through your lineage for generations, as constant as the rising sun. We, [Name], cannot bear to restrain our gaze upon your golden countenance and offer these most sincere and earnest prayers.
Regarding the phrase "plunged in mire and charcoal" (*tútàn*), the commentary states: "Mire is mud; charcoal is fire.
Jie, though the ruler of the people, instead acted with darkness and chaos, casting the people into mire and charcoal. Having thus lost that which made him their ruler.

Regarding "execution and slaughter," the *Lüxíng* (Punishments of Lü) of the Book of Documents says: "The execution and slaughter of the innocent. Regarding "floodwaters," Mencius says: "In the time of Yao..."
At that time, the world was not yet at peace; the deluge flowed across the land, overflowing everywhere.
